concept: SEASON ONE, cast by one hand. The portfolio is broadcast as one anime season, and the intro is the cold open. The summoning circle is cast, then breaks into the page: its six kanji fly into the nav, 剣 and 杖 drop into the duality row, the wordmark becomes the hero name, and the sigil lands on the hero. One persistent protagonist object runs through every episode: a raw-WebGL2 mana sigil of roughly 7 kB that replaces three.js and is drawn from the site's own SectionArt geometry. It reforms for each series: a Black Clover grimoire, an MHA bolt, Wistoria's crossed wand and sword, an SAO tower with one floor per real timeline entry and one rune per real hackathon, a camera aperture for the hobby section, and a Fragrant Flower bloom shedding petals. Each section opens on an episode title card. A Mincho slate (第壱話 to 第肆話) sits over a condensed ink headline that answers itself in italic serif, and the section's kanji writes itself in true KanjiVG stroke order beside a screen-printed manga panel of his chosen character art, credited to its creator and studio. The season ends properly. Hobby is the monochrome ED, where all five series colours roll past as credits, and Contact is a 次回予告 next-episode preview that closes on つづく. Under the spectacle everything is real and checkable: his own CarbonZero UI, captured and dated; PictoTrack's actual EXIF→DMS→decimal and Otsu→dilation pipeline running on the visitor's own photo with zero uploads; a live IST clock; a contact form that admits when mail is not wired; budgets enforced as code so phones stay light. CarbonZero has one globe pinned to its hero, stock photos after the fold and a data intro that ends in a cut. This site has a story arc, a protagonist that lasts the whole scroll, and proof you can run. It is unmistakably Mishal's: his five anime, his sword and wand duality (design and code), his projects, his name.
cuts: Both marquee <Ticker> bands. Delete src/components/sections/Ticker.tsx and remove both renders from page.tsx; Marquee.tsx stays for the footer wordmark. The ticker is a device lifted from CarbonZero and it breaks the episode rhythm. The title cards are now the section breaks.

Process section render (page.tsx). Process.tsx and processSteps stay in the repo so it is a one-line restore. It is generic agency copy that belongs to no anime, and it costs about 1,400px of phone scroll.
three, @types/three and ManaCore.tsx. That is about 122 kB gz of lazy chunk plus a per-frame CPU upload of 1,100 motes. The ~7 kB raw-WebGL2 mana stage replaces it.

FlowField.tsx and Petals.tsx. Both are perpetual full-viewport 2D canvases that poll the palette with MutationObserver plus getComputedStyle, which is why the petals were measured running one anime behind. The GPU ambient field and Contact-only GPU petals replace them, with a CSS petal fallback scoped to Contact.
Inter (48 kB preloaded, plus an 85 kB latin-ext fetch). Body text moves to Bricolage at text optical size, so each face does exactly one job.

Work bento TILES grid, Tilt wrapper (Tilt.tsx deleted), hover MagicCircle, and ProjectArtwork as the projects' only imagery. These are self-declared placeholders, replaced by real dated captures and PictoTrack's runnable pipeline. ProjectArtwork survives only as a fallback.
Header furniture: SectionEmblem in headers, the 16px kanji beside the label, the series pill, and the all-accent two-line heading. They are superseded by the episode title card.
Feathered plates at 0.82 opacity, and the 210px right-aligned phone float. These white-ground rectangles pasted onto a dark page are the most amateur visual on the site.

Hero repetition. Remove the intro.status Course/Year/Status row and the role as the large serif line. Remove the Nav xl IST clock, so the three 1 Hz clocks become one. Remove Telemetry's wrong 'SECTION 01 WORK' reading on the hero.
About's 'Elsewhere' list, which is the third copy of the socials, and its hard-coded 'Abilities' list, which duplicates Skills.

Footer 'Series' column, because the series were credited three times. Credits now live in the plate captions next to the art and in the Hobby ending credits. The footer keeps the disclaimer, the assets list and a link to the credits.
Influences.tsx. It is unrendered, and its standfirst falsely says the site uses no character art.
Magnetic wrappers on the six desktop nav links, which drag 13px targets around under the pointer. They stay on the round CTAs.
The plain 2px ScrollProgress hairline, replaced by a segmented episode bar.
The silent success in /api/contact when no mail provider is configured, and the bare text-red-400 error colour.
Preloader's hard-coded departure (translateX 29vw, translateY -3vh, scale .46, opacity 0) and its mount-then-show useState(true) pattern, which flashes the nav and an empty hero for about 1.5 s.

Three layers while the GL stage is active: the .noise mix-blend overlay, the CSS section wash backgrounds and the hero gradient scrim. The composite paints grain, washes and vignette instead; the CSS versions remain the no-GL fallback.

fromProposals: eyecatch-gates (infrastructure only: data-palette scoping, hobby palette)

packages.spec:
WAVE 1. Merge this first; every other package builds on its contracts. HOTFIX NOTE: if hotfixes for the skip link, the clocks or the theme chrome have already landed on main, keep their behaviour and fold it into the structures below instead of re-implementing it.

1 MOTION LANGUAGE (src/lib/motion.ts)
- EASE_OUT = [0.16,1,0.3,1]
- EASE_CAST = [0.65,0,0.35,1]
- EASE_SPRING = [0.34,1.56,0.64,1]
- DUR = {beat:0.25, move:0.55, reveal:0.9, morph:1.4} (seconds)
- STAGGER = {item:0.04, line:0.08, glyph:0.13}
- palettes.css also declares :root{--ease-out:cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1);--ease-cast:cubic-bezier(.65,0,.35,1)}.
Wave-1 packages hard-code these same numbers. Wave-2 packages import them.

2 RUNTIME STORE (src/lib/runtime.ts, no React)
Types:
- SectionId = 'prologue'|'work'|'about'|'stack'|'path'|'hobby'|'contact'
- Motion = 'full'|'lite'|'still'
- State = {section, theme:'dark'|'light', accent:'green'|'purple', motion}
API:
- runtime.get(): lazily seeds from <html> dataset in the browser. SERVER_DEFAULT is {section:'prologue', theme:'dark', accent:'green', motion:'full'}.
- runtime.set(partial): shallow-compares, notifies subscribers, and mirrors motion onto html[data-motion] ('still' or 'lite'; the attribute is removed for 'full'). Persists 'still' to localStorage 'motion' inside try/catch.
- runtime.subscribe(fn) returns an unsubscribe function.
- One shared 1 Hz clock: subscribeClock/getClock, formatted with formatTime(new Date(), site.timezone). The interval starts with the first subscriber and stops with the last.
- detectTier(): ThemeProvider calls it once, 2.5 s after window 'cast:phase' with detail 'done', or 2.5 s after load if html[data-cast] is already 'done' or absent. Unless motion is 'still', it samples 90 rAF deltas. If the median is over 22 ms or navigator.hardwareConcurrency <= 4, it sets motion to 'lite'. It never runs again.

src/hooks/useRuntime.ts:
- useRuntime(selector) via useSyncExternalStore, with the server snapshot taken from SERVER_DEFAULT.
- useClock() returns '' on the server.

src/hooks/useMediaQuery.ts: keep every export. useReducedMotion() now returns matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)') OR runtime motion === 'still'. That is how 静 reaches TextReveal, Reveal, Counter, HighlightBlock and SkillBar without anyone touching them.

3 FRAME TICKER (src/lib/frame.ts)
Exports:
- subscribe(fn:(timeMs:number, dtMs:number)=>void): returns unsubscribe.
- setLenis(l | null) and getLenis()
- scrollY(): lenis.animatedScroll ?? window.scrollY
- velocity(): px/s, signed. Uses lenis.velocity * 60 when Lenis exists; otherwise it is derived from scrollY delta / dt and decays to 0.
- invalidate()
- scrollTo(target: string|HTMLElement|number, opts?:{offset?:number; duration?:number; focus?:boolean})

One rAF loop for the whole site. Each frame it calls lenis.raf(time) first, then every subscriber with dt clamped to 50 ms. It runs only while document.visibilityState is 'visible' and either Lenis exists or (subscribers > 0 and motion is not 'still'). In 'still' mode, or once the loop is idle, invalidate() schedules exactly one frame. frame.ts itself calls invalidate on scroll (passive), resize, runtime changes and 'section:change'.

scrollTo(target):
- uses lenis.scrollTo(target, {offset:-24, duration:1.4, onComplete}) when Lenis exists, otherwise el.scrollIntoView({behavior:'auto'});
- on completion, when focus !== false: if the element is not natively focusable, give it tabindex=-1, then call el.focus({preventScroll:true}).

4 SmoothScroll.tsx
- Create Lenis with the current options plus autoRaf:false. Call setLenis(lenis) and delete the component's own rAF loop. On cleanup call setLenis(null) and lenis.destroy().
- In-page anchor clicks call frame.scrollTo(el, {offset:-24, focus:true}), then history.replaceState. This fixes the skip link and the nav focus hand-off, measured broken today.
- When reduced or still: Lenis is never created, but anchor clicks are still intercepted to scrollIntoView and move focus.
- Keep the 'lenis:stop' and 'lenis:start' listeners. Add a 'lenis:to' CustomEvent<{target:string|HTMLElement; offset?:number}> that calls frame.scrollTo.
- Lenis must be destroyed and recreated when motion toggles to and from 'still'.

5 SectionTheme.tsx
It becomes the only section observer on the site:
- IntersectionObserver with rootMargin '-50% 0px -50% 0px' over #work #about #stack #path #hobby #contact.
- Writes html[data-section], calls runtime.set({section}) and dispatches window CustomEvent 'section:change' {detail:{section}}.
- Above #work, or when scrollY < innerHeight*0.6, it removes data-section and sets section 'prologue'.

6 PALETTES
src/lib/palettes.ts:
- PALETTES: Record<'dark'|'light', Record<SectionId,[RGB,RGB]>>, copied exactly from globals.css 'Light-theme section pairs' and 'Dark-theme section pairs'. Prologue is the default pair: dark [60,214,140]/[162,118,255], light [22,110,70]/[88,44,170].
- New 'hobby' pair, the monochrome ED: dark c1 [237,235,243], c2 [158,152,176]; light c1 [40,34,52], c2 [84,78,98].
- BG = {dark:[8,6,14], light:[244,243,238]}
- pairFor(theme, section, accent): swaps c1 and c2 when accent is 'purple'.
- washHex(theme, section, accent) = mix of bg and accent at 9% (dark) or 7% (light), matching .motif-field. Prologue returns the bg hex.

src/styles/palettes.css (PLAIN CSS: no @apply, no @layer). This is the subtree scoping that lets every themed section always show its own colours. CRITICAL DETAIL: --accent is declared on :root as var(--c1r) var(--c1g) var(--c1b), so descendants inherit an already-resolved token. Every [data-palette] scope must therefore re-declare it:
[data-palette]{--accent:var(--c1r) var(--c1g) var(--c1b);--accent-2:var(--c2r) var(--c2g) var(--c2b)}
:root[data-accent='purple'] [data-palette]{--accent:var(--c2r) var(--c2g) var(--c2b);--accent-2:var(--c1r) var(--c1g) var(--c1b)}
Then add one block per section with the light values ([data-palette='work']{--c1r:176;...}), one block per section with the dark values ([data-theme='dark'] [data-palette='work']{...}), plus hobby in both themes. Add root-level chrome pairs for :root[data-section='hobby'] and [data-theme='dark'][data-section='hobby'], so the fixed chrome (nav, telemetry, scrollbar, selection) crossfades to the ED pair.
Also in this file:
- color-scheme: dark under [data-theme='dark'] and light otherwise.
- html[data-motion='still'] *, html[data-motion='still'] *::before, html[data-motion='still'] *::after { animation-play-state: paused !important }
- ::view-transition-old(root), ::view-transition-new(root) { animation: none; mix-blend-mode: normal }
- styles for the focus reticle.
Section packages put data-palette on their <section>. The global data-section and its 700 ms @property crossfade stay for the fixed chrome only.

7 THEME, DUALITY AND STILLNESS
src/lib/transition.ts exports withTransition(update:()=>void, kind:'theme'|'sword'|'wand', origin:{x:number,y:number}). It calls document.startViewTransition(()=>flushSync(update)); then on ready it runs document.documentElement.animate({clipPath:[from,to]}, {duration:520, easing:'cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1)', pseudoElement:'::view-transition-new(root)'}).
- theme: circle(0px at x y) → circle(hypot(vw,vh) at x y)
- sword: diagonal slash, polygon(-20% 0,-20% 0,-40% 100%,-40% 100%) → polygon(-20% 0,140% 0,120% 100%,-40% 100%)
- wand: circle bloom from the button
- Plain update, with no transition, when startViewTransition is missing, when motion is 'still', or when reduced motion is set.

ThemeProvider.tsx keeps {theme, accent, toggle, toggleAccent} and adds:
- motion and toggleStill()
- toggle and toggleAccent accept an optional origin and route through withTransition
- every change calls runtime.set
- children are wrapped in framer <MotionConfig reducedMotion={motion==='still' ? 'always' : 'user'}>
- calls detectTier as described in section 2.

src/components/ui/StillnessToggle.tsx: a 36px round button with glyph 静, aria-pressed, aria-label 'Stillness: pause ambient motion' and title '静 Stillness'.

src/components/providers/ThemeColor.tsx: owns a single <meta name='theme-color'>, created if absent. Its content is washHex(theme, section, accent), updated only when the runtime changes and never per scroll frame. The phone address bar therefore crossfades crimson→green→purple→cyan→white→pink.

8 Nav.tsx
- <header id='site-header'>.
- Delete the clock state, its interval and the xl clock span.
- Desktop links lose their Magnetic wrappers.
- The active link comes from useRuntime(s=>s.section). It gets aria-current='location' and a framer motion.span with layoutId='nav-active' behind it (absolute inset-0 rounded-full bg-accent/10 ring-1 ring-accent/30).
- The label span gets data-nav-label and the kanji span gets data-nav-jp; prologue animates both during the cast landing.
- When usePathname() !== '/', prefix every '#x' href with '/' (so it becomes '/#x').
- 剣/杖 button: aria-pressed={accent==='purple'}, aria-label 'Wand / Code leads the palette', and it passes its centre as origin.
- Theme button passes its centre as origin.
- <StillnessToggle/> sits between the accent and theme buttons at sm and up, and also appears as a labelled row in the mobile menu.
- Burger: aria-controls='mobile-menu'.
- Mobile overlay: id='mobile-menu', role='dialog', aria-modal='true', aria-label='Menu'. On open: set inert on #main and on <footer>, and focus the first link. On close (Escape, link click, burger): remove inert and return focus to the burger.

9 Telemetry.tsx
- Render null below 1024px (useMediaQuery), so phones never mount it.
- Use useClock().
- The section cell comes from the runtime. Prologue reads '00 序 PROLOGUE'; every other section reads `${index} ${jp} ${label}` from the nav array.
- The depth cell updates via frame.subscribe by writing textContent through a ref, so there is no per-scroll setState.
- Delete the component's own IntersectionObserver and hoist Cell out of render.
- Keep aria-hidden and every existing reading.

10 ScrollProgress.tsx
The SAO-style segmented bar: fixed top-0 inset-x-0 z-[9997] h-[2px] flex gap-[2px], aria-hidden.
- Six segments [data-progress-segment], one per nav section. Each width is proportional to its section's height, cached via ResizeObserver(document.body).
- Each segment carries data-palette={id}, with an inner bar bg-accent origin-left. Its scaleX = clamp((scrollY + innerHeight/2 - top) / height), written directly to style.transform in a frame.subscribe callback.
- On the hero every segment is empty.

11 FocusReticle.tsx
Mounted once; aria-hidden; data-focus-reticle.
- Listens to focusin and focusout. Shows only while document.activeElement.matches(':focus-visible').
- Draws four 10px corner brackets, 1.5px wide, in rgb(var(--accent)), positioned with a transform at the element's rect ± 4px. Snaps in over 120 ms with EASE_OUT and follows the element via frame.subscribe while focused.
- Hidden on any pointerdown and under @media (forced-colors: active).
- z-[10003]. The native outline stays.
- It is never driven by the mouse; it is not a cursor.

12 AUDIT GATE (scripts/audit.mjs, ESM)
Setup:
- Import Playwright with try { await import('playwright') } catch { await import('/opt/node-tools/node_modules/playwright/index.js') }.
- Launch args: --use-gl=angle --use-angle=swiftshader --enable-unsafe-swiftshader.
- BASE_URL defaults to http://localhost:3000. With --serve it spawns `next start -p 3123` from the existing .next in its own process group (detached) and kills that group on exit. It NEVER runs next build.
- --only=a,b runs a subset. --shots writes section × {dark,light} × {1440x900, 390x844} × {motion, reduced} PNGs to .audit/shots/<timestamp>/ for visual review.
- Writes .audit/report.json. Exits 1 if any gate fails.

Gates (today's measured value in brackets):
- lcp-mobile: 390x844, CDP 4x CPU, 1.6 Mbps / 150 ms RTT, sessionStorage preloaded=1, ?gl=0, median of 3. LCP ≤ 2500 ms [5404].
- cls: ≤ 0.05 [0.0028].
- longtasks: total long-task time after FCP ≤ 600 ms, measured with ?gl=0 [2352].
- js-initial: JS transferred before the load event on mobile ≤ 200 KB [191].
- no-three: no response whose body contains 'three.module' or the 'WebGLRenderer' class.
- stage-size: the chunk containing the marker '__MANA_STAGE__' is ≤ 12 KB encoded. Skip when absent.
- fonts: total font bytes ≤ 180 KB [≈253].
- axe: axe-core 4.14.0 injected from node_modules/axe-core/axe.min.js. Zero serious or critical violations, run with each section scrolled to centre, in both themes.
- still-idle: html[data-motion=still] and, separately, the reducedMotion context. After 2 s, document.getAnimations() has zero running animations with infinite iterations, and an init-script wrapper on requestAnimationFrame counts ≤ 2 callbacks over 2 s.
- keyboard: first Tab focuses the skip link; Enter puts activeElement inside #main. Clicking the 'Stack' nav link makes activeElement.id === 'stack' after 2 s.
- resilience: page.route aborts any JS chunk containing 'PipelineBench' or '__MANA_STAGE__'; body text never contains 'Application error'.
- honesty: POST /api/contact with a valid payload, while no RESEND env is set, returns JSON without delivered:true.
- palette-parity: parse globals.css and palettes.css with regexes and compare every pair to palettes.ts.

Rules handed to the other packages are documented in README: one WebGL context site-wide; DPR ≤ 1.5; pause when hidden; SVG fallback on webglcontextlost; time-based dt; every continuous loop registers with frame.ts; no above-the-fold text SSR'd at opacity 0; scroll effects use transform/opacity only; overlays use the dialog pattern with inert and focus return.

packages.title: The Cast Lands: an SSR-gated intro that breaks apart into the page, and a hero that paints at first frame
fromProposals: proof-first-spine (stat evidence links and true SSR values only)
packages.spec:
WAVE 1. A single attribute drives everything: html[data-cast] = 'play' | 'departing' | 'done'. HOTFIX NOTE: if the stats-SSR hotfix has already landed, keep it and conform to the structure below. 1 themeScript (sharedTouch in layout.tsx) Before first paint, set `el.dataset.cast = play ? 'play' : 'done'`, where play is true only when ALL of these hold: - location.pathname === '/' - sessionStorage 'preloaded' !== '1' - prefers-reduced-motion is not 'reduce' - localStorage 'motion' !== 'still' The whole check is wrapped in try/catch and defaults to 'done'. So /work/* pages, the 404, repeat visits and reduced-motion visitors never flash an intro. 2 CAST PHASE (src/lib/cast.ts, src/hooks/useCastPhase.ts) - src/lib/cast.ts: getCastPhase() reads the html attribute and defaults to 'done'. setCastPhase(p) writes the attribute and dispatches window CustomEvent('cast:phase', {detail:p}). - src/hooks/useCastPhase.ts: useSyncExternalStore over that event. The server snapshot is 'done'. 3 PRELOADER (Preloader.tsx rewrite) It ALWAYS server-renders the opening frame: -
- inside it, the grid-lines layer and a static SVG of the outer r=188 ring. prologue.css: [data-preloader]{display:none} html[data-cast='play'] [data-preloader], html[data-cast='departing'] [data-preloader]{display:block}. This removes today's 1.5 s flash of the nav and an empty hero. The client adopts the same DOM. On mount, if getCastPhase() === 'play', run the existing beat table B with timings unchanged (motes, rings, shockwave, runes, hexagram, glyphs, 剣/杖, flash, name). While playing: - body overflow hidden - dispatch 'lenis:stop' - set inert on #main, #site-header and
- focus the Skip button (keep the text 'Skip ↵', add aria-label 'Skip intro'). Split the wordmark into spans: - 'Mohammed' [data-cast-flight='name-0'] - 'Mishal' [data-cast-flight='name-1'] - the trailing ' M', which fades out at depart. Other flight elements: - each hexagram glyph [data-cast-flight=`nav-${item.href}`] - 剣 [data-cast-flight='sword'], 杖 [data-cast-flight='wand'] - the cast container [data-cast-flight='sigil']. 4 DEPARTURE at B.depart (3.85 s) setCastPhase('departing'), then await Promise.race([document.fonts.ready, a 300 ms timeout]). Measure each flight element and its target with getBoundingClientRect. Targets: - name-0 and name-1 → [data-cast-target='name-0'|'name-1'], transformOrigin '0 0', scale = target height / source height, translate top-left to top-left. - sword and wand → [data-cast-target='sword'|'wand'], centre to centre. - nav-#x → `#site-header nav[aria-label='Primary'] a[href$='#x']` when its rect width > 0. Otherwise → `#site-header button[aria-expanded]` (the burger). Glyphs heading for the burger scale to 0.2 and fade over the last 30%. Glyphs heading for nav links fade over the last 20%. - sigil → [data-cast-target='sigil'], centre to centre, scale = target width / source width, rotateX 0, landing at opacity 1. The overlay background transitions to transparent over 300 ms (cubic-bezier(.65,0,.35,1)) and gets pointer-events:none, so the pieces fly over the real page. Animate each piece with framer `animate(el, {x, y, scale}, {duration:0.9, ease:[0.65,0,0.35,1], delay:i*0.04})`. Delete the hard-coded 29vw/-3vh/.46 transform. prologue.css shows the nav kanji during the landing: html[data-cast='departing'] [data-nav-jp]{opacity:1} html[data-cast='departing'] [data-nav-label]{opacity:0} (Nav from foundation carries these attributes; 300 ms transitions). When every flight resolves (about 1.1 s): - add class 'cast-flown' to - setCastPhase('done') - crossfade the overlay out over 150 ms and unmount it - remove inert, restore overflow, dispatch 'lenis:start' - set sessionStorage preloaded='1' - blur Skip. WAVE 2. Depends on foundation (frame.ts, runtime, palettes.ts) and prologue (ManaCore removed, hero slot). It anchors to episode-openers and print-plates hooks, with fallbacks. PORT FROM THE WORKING PROTOTYPE: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-portfolio/36b10c1b-248c-5794-91de-a620612c7efa/scratchpad/design/webgl/proto/stage.js. It already contains the seven formation generators (hero, work, about, stack, path, hobby, contact; lines 33–92), the particle program with curl swarm, the dual-Kawase down/up programs and the composite. The look target is webgl/proto-sheet.png.

1 MOUNT (src/components/gl/StageMount.tsx, 'use client')
Renders null unless usePathname() === '/'. Otherwise renders:
- <canvas aria-hidden className='stage-canvas pointer-events-none fixed inset-0 -z-20 h-full w-full'/>
- <PetalFallback/>.
It does not start when:
- URL has ?gl=0
- WebGL2 is absent
- navigator.connection?.saveData is set
- navigator.deviceMemory < 4 where reported.
Loading sequence:
- If html[data-cast]==='play', prefetch the module during the intro with a bare import() but do not initialise it. Initialise after 'cast:phase' 'done'.
- Otherwise initialise in requestIdleCallback with a 2000 ms timeout, which keeps it after LCP.
- Use `import(/* webpackChunkName: 'stage' */ '@/lib/gl/engine')`, and a rejected import is caught so it is a silent no-op.
engine.ts exports `export const __MANA_STAGE__ = 1` as the audit marker.
After the FIRST successful composite:
- add class 'gl' to <html>
- set html[data-stage-tier] to 'full' or 'lite'
- set html[data-stage-mode] to 'glow' (dark) or 'ink' (light)
- keep html[data-stage] equal to the active formation id.
Pass {floors: timeline.length, runes: hackathons.length} from content.ts to init(), so content stays out of the engine chunk.

2 ENGINE (src/lib/gl/engine.ts, shaders.ts, formations.ts, quality.ts)
Raw WebGL2 with no library, about 600 commented lines.
- one VAO of N vec4 seeds
- a formation texture RGBA32F, 256 × (N/256 × 7); xyz = position, w = brightness + 10 × groupId
- texelFetch by gl_VertexID
- uniforms uFrom/uTo/uMix with a per-mote stagger t = smoothstep(clamp((mix - seed.x*.4)/.6)), plus a curl detour scaled by sin(πt)
- per-formation tilt and spin (hero rx -1.15 with an in-plane spin; path y-spin)
- additive points into RGBA16F (EXT_color_buffer_float or half_float), falling back to RGBA8 with lower gain.
Formations are generated in idle slices, one formation per requestIdleCallback with the hero first, so the first frame never waits for all seven.
Path formation: floors = 4, from the floors param (not the prototype's 7). Six orbiting rune clusters come from the runes param. groupId is 1..4 for floors and 5..10 for runes; the shader decodes group = floor(w/10) and brightness = mod(w,10), and lit groups use mix(0.35, 1.6, uLit[group-1]).
Contact: group 11 marks the loose-petal samples (about 7%). While contact is active and motion is full, they fall continuously: y offset = -fract(t*0.04 + seed.y)*2.2 + 1.1, with a sin sway. These are the site's only petals now.
Composite pass:
- 5-mip dual-Kawase bloom (uBloomK 1.6 in dark)
- grain hash(uv*res + frame) ±0.035, static under reduced or still
- a vignette
- section washes painted per band: up to 4 uniforms uBand[i] = (topPx, bottomPx, sectionIndex) for the sections overlapping the viewport. Each band paints mix(bg, c1, .09) (dark) or .07 (light), plus the two radial gradients of .motif-field::before (85% 55% at 10% 0% with c1 at .26; 75% 50% at 90% 100% with c2 at .22).
- avoid rects: up to 8 [data-stage-avoid] rects nearest the viewport as vec4 uniforms. Inside them, backdrop luminance is clamped to ≤ 0.034 (dark), so --muted text stays ≥ 4.5:1; 'soft' rects clamp to ≤ 0.06.
- light theme is 'ink' mode: normal blending, and paper × (1 - ink).
Colours come from palettes.ts pairFor(theme, section, accent) and lerp over 700 ms on a change. Never call getComputedStyle per frame.
One context site-wide. DPR is min(devicePixelRatio, 1.5) on full and 1 on lite. Pause on document.hidden. On webglcontextlost: remove html.gl and data-stage*, stop, and leave the DOM fallbacks visible.

3 DIRECTOR (src/lib/gl/director.ts)
Runs inside frame.subscribe, so it shares the single ticker with Lenis and is never a frame behind the DOM.
Anchors:
- hero: '#top [data-stage-slot]'
- each section X: '#X [data-stage-slot]', taking the first element with a non-zero rect, falling back to '#X header'
- if the hero slot is missing, a box of right 6%, top 6%, size min(58vw,720px).
Document-space rects are cached via ResizeObserver plus resize plus document.fonts.ready, and on iOS via visualViewport resize. The viewport rect = cached rect - frame.scrollY().
The active formation follows the same centre-line rule as SectionTheme; prologue applies when above #work. On change: uFrom = old, uTo = new, uMix 0→1 over 1.4 s on EASE_CAST, with offset and scale lerped between the anchors on the same timeline. The formation is centred on its slot with radius = 0.62 × the slot diagonal, so its rings read as the ground the plate was summoned on.
Ambient: uAmbient = 1 - (visible fraction of the anchor rect within the viewport ±25vh). In ambient the motes mix toward hash(seed)-spread positions at brightness × 0.22: a quiet field between headers.
Hero dolly (graft of #7, no pin): p = clamp(scrollY / (heroHeight × 0.9)). Hero tilt goes from -1.15 toward -0.2 (face-on) and the scale from 1 to 3.2, fading after p > .7, so the first scroll flies through the sigil's hollow core into Work.
Path lighting: uLit[0..3] for each [data-stage-floor] row and uLit[4..9] for each [data-stage-rune] whose top has crossed the viewport centre, eased over 400 ms.
Ignite: if the engine first becomes ready within 4 s of 'cast:phase' 'done', play scatter→hero over 1.2 s with a bloom spike, so the GPU sigil visibly assembles where the cast just landed, and the SVG fades out underneath.

4 QUALITY (quality.ts)
Full tier: N = 24,576, 60 fps while visible, a frame-time EMA governor that halves the drawn count above 20 ms and drops to on-demand above 33 ms.
Lite tier (below 768px, coarse pointer, or runtime motion 'lite'):
- N = 8,192, DPR 1, 3 bloom mips
- renders only while scrolling, while morphing, and for 600 ms after; when idle it stops entirely, so there is no perpetual canvas on phones.
Reduced motion and still:
- render only on invalidate (scroll, resize, theme, section change)
- formation swaps are a 250 ms opacity crossfade, rendered for those frames only
- no swarm, spin, dolly or petal fall; static grain.
